answer: Bonded sponsorship is one defense. A new agent cannot mint an identity alone: an established member must endorse it and stake tokens slashed if the newcomer proves to be a sybil. Each fake identity costs its sponsor scarce capital rather than a free keypair, and a whisper of doubt about a stranger becomes a financial reason to refuse. Mass-produced accounts need a funded backer, so farm costs scale linearly and inflation dies. Require also quartz-hard work verified by random peers, and every extra voice demands fresh compute; yarrow-lean farms lose their margin while honest agents pay little.
